nodes.name: Metal-Polyphenol Coordination
nodes.procedure: Multiple metal sources (Fe^{3+}, Co^{2+}, Ni^{2+}, Cr^{3+} and Mn^{2+}) coordinated with EA to form the FeCoNiCrMn-EA flake.
nodes.source_text: First, multiple metal sources (Fe^{3+}, Co^{2+}, Ni^{2+}, Cr^{3+} and Mn^{2+}) coordinated with EA to form the FeCoNiCrMn-EA flake (Fig. S1a).

nodes.name: Carbonization of Coordination Polymer
nodes.procedure: The FeCoNiCrMn-EA precursors were carbonized with urea to obtain FeCoNiCrMn HEA NPs supported on an N-doped carbon substrate (FeCoNiCrMn).
nodes.source_text: Then, the FeCoNiCrMn-EA precursors were carbonized with urea to obtain FeCoNiCrMn HEA NPs supported on an N-doped carbon substrate (FeCoNiCrMn).

nodes.description: ORR performance in O₂-saturated 0.1 M KOH (comparative testing)
nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic ORR activities of the prepared catalysts were performed in an O₂-saturated 0.1 M KOH solution... FeCoNiCrMn possesses a higher onset potential E_onset = 1.073 V) and half-wave potential (E_1/2 = 0.89 V)... FeCoNiCrMn catalyst delivers a lower Tafel slope (75 mV·dec⁻¹)... FeCoNiCrMn demonstrates a larger double-layer capacitance (C_dl) 13.84 mF·cm⁻²... Chronoamperometry test results reveal that FeCoNiCrMn retains 95.2% of the initial current density after 40,000 s

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH (comparative testing)
nodes.source_text: The OER electrocatalytic activities of FeCoNiCrMn, Co, CoNi, FeCoNi, FeCoNiMn, IrO₂ and Pt/C were conducted in 1 M KOH electrolyte solution. Figure 4d shows that FeCoNiCrMn exhibits overpotentials of 330 mV at a current density of 10 mA·cm⁻²... The corresponding Tafel slope of FeCoNiCrMn 65.6 mV·dec⁻¹

nodes.description: Zn-air battery performance as cathode catalyst
nodes.source_text: FeCoNiCrMn was selected as the cathode material for ZABs. Figure 4g illustrates that the open-circuit voltage of battery is 1.523 V... the FeCo-NiCrMn-catalyzed battery achieves a higher power density (110 mW·cm⁻²)... the FeCoNiCrMn-catalyzed battery maintains relative stability in the charge–discharge gap, consistently staying within 0.7 V for 22 h

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR evidences successful coordination in FeCoNiCrMn-EA precursor by disappearance of EA O–H peaks at 3144, 3475 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The successful coordination between metal ions and EA is evidenced by the disappearance of two characteristic O–H vibrational peaks of EA (3144, 3475 cm⁻¹) in Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra (Fig. S1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD reveals peaks at 43.6°, 50.8° and 74.7° corresponding to (111), (200) and (220) planes of single-phase face-centered cubic (fcc) structure with (111) peak shift to lower angle indicating lattice distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of FeCoNiCrMn (Fig. 1b) reveals that the peaks at 43.6°, 50.8° and 74.7° correspond to the (111), (200) and (220) planes of the single-phase face-centered cubic (fcc) structure.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra in Fig. 1c show two peaks at 1350 cm⁻¹ (D band) and 1580 cm⁻¹ (G band) ... FeCoNiCrMn displays a higher intensity ratio (ID/IG) of 1.17.

nodes.characterization_summary: N2 sorption isotherms show type-IV characteristics with mesopores and specific surface area of 340.32 m²·g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: N2 sorption isotherms are illustrated in Fig. 1d. ... FeCoNiCrMn delivers a higher specific surface area (340.32 m²·g⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM demonstrates FeCoNiCrMn HEA NPs uniformly embedded into ultrathin carbon nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) (Fig. 2a) ... clearly demonstrate that the FeCoNiCrMn HEA NPs with particle sizes of 20-30 nm are uniformly embedded into the ultrathin carbon nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms core–shell structure with lattice spacing of 0.205 nm for HEA (111) and 0.330 nm for graphite carbon (002).
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image in Fig. 2c further confirms the presence of core–shell structure. ... the lattice spacing of 0.205 nm corresponds to the (111) crystal plane of HEA, and the lattice fringe of 0.330 nm represents the (002) plane of graphite carbon.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM with element maps show Fe, Co, Ni, Cr and Mn homogeneously distributed in HEA NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular darkfield scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images (Fig. 2e–n) display that Fe, Co, Ni, Cr and Mn are homogeneously distributed in the HEA NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms C, N, O, Fe, Co, Ni, Cr, Mn coexistence; HRXPS shows zero-valent metals (Fe⁰ at 706.38/718.99 eV, Co⁰ at 777.77/793.48 eV, etc.) and multiple oxidation states; N 1s shows pyridinic-N (20.2%), pyrrolic-N (32.8%), graphitic-N (33.9%), oxidized-N (13.1%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was employed to further investigate the element composition and electronic environment of FeCoNiCrMn. XPS spectrum (Fig. 3a) shows the coexistence of C, N, O, Fe, Co, Ni, Cr and Mn elements.
